blocks.title: Human Excretory System
blocks.text:
Core Concept

Nephron is the structural and functional unit of kidney. It is an epithelial tube which is about 3 cm long and 20-60 m in diameter.

blocks.title: QUESTION 1
blocks.question:
Read the following statements about human excretory system and choose the correct option accordingly.

I. Kidneys are reddish brown and bean- shaped structure.

II. Kidneys are situated between the last thoracic to third lumbar vertebra.

III. Each kidney of an adult human measures 10-12 cm in length, 5-7 cm in  width, 2-3 cm thickness, and average weight 120-170 gram.

(1) I and II

(2) II and III

(3) III and I

(4) All
blocks.answer:
Answer = 4

Explanation:

All the statements provided about the human excretory system are correct:

  • I. Kidneys are reddish brown and bean-shaped structure.
This is true. The kidneys have a reddish-brown color and a distinct bean shape.
  • II. Kidneys are situated between the last thoracic to third lumbar vertebra.
This is also correct. The kidneys are located in the lumbar region, specifically between the last thoracic vertebra and the third lumbar vertebra in the lower back.
  • III. Each kidney of an adult human measures 10-12 cm in length, 5-7 cm in width, 2-3 cm thickness, and average weight 120-170 gram.
This is accurate. The dimensions and weight of the kidneys fall within the stated ranges for an adult human.

blocks.title: QUESTION.2
blocks.question:
Given below are statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the  options given below :

Assertion (A) : Nephrons are of two types :Cortical & Juxta medullary, based on their relative position in cortex and medulla.

Reason (R): Juxta medullary nephrons have short loop of Henle whereas,  cortical nephrons have a longer loop of Henle.

(1) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

(2) A is true but R is false.

(3) A is false but R is true.

(4) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
blocks.answer:
Answer = 2

Explanation:

Assertion A:

"Nephrons are of two types: Cortical & Juxtamedullary, based on their relative position in cortex and medulla."

This is true. Nephrons are classified into:

Cortical nephrons: Located mainly in the renal cortex.

Juxtamedullary nephrons: Situated near the medulla, with their loops of Henle extending deep into the medulla.

Reason R:

"Juxtamedullary nephrons have short loops of Henle, whereas cortical nephrons have a longer loop of Henle."

This is false. The opposite is true:

Juxtamedullary nephrons have long loops of Henle that extend deep into the medulla, allowing them to concentrate urine effectively.

Cortical nephrons have short loops of Henle and are primarily involved in basic filtration.

blocks.title: Question.1
blocks.question:
Which of the following factors is responsible for the formation of concentrated urine?

(1) Low levels of antidiuretic hormone.

(2) Maintaining hyperosmolarity towards inner medullary interstitium in the  kidneys.

(3) Secretion of erythropoietin by juxtaglomerular complex.

(4) Hydrostatic pressure during glomerular filtration.
blocks.answer:
Answer = 2

Explanation:

The ability to form concentrated urine depends on :

Hyperosmolarity of the medullary interstitium :

The kidney maintains a hyperosmolar environment in the medullary interstitium due to the countercurrent mechanism between the loop of Henle and the vasa recta. This high osmolarity draws water out of the collecting ducts concentrating the urine.
options: (2) Maintaining hyperosmolarity towards inner medullary interstitium in the  kidneys.
(3) Secretion of erythropoietin by juxtaglomerular complex.

blocks.title: Question.3
blocks.question:
Which of the following factors is responsible for the formation of concentrated urine?

(1) Low levels of antidiuretic hormone.

(2) Maintaining hyperosmolarity towards inner medullary interstitium in the kidneys.

(3) Secretion of erythropoietin by juxtaglomerular complex.

(4) Hydrostatic pressure during glomerular filtration.
blocks.answer:
Answer = 2

Explanation:

The formation of concentrated urine relies on the kidneys' ability to reabsorb water while excreting solutes. The hyperosmolarity of the medullary interstitium is critical for this process and is maintained by:

  • The countercurrent multiplier mechanism in the loop of Henle, which actively transports solutes into the medulla.
  • The countercurrent exchanger in the vasa recta, which preserves the osmotic gradient.
  • The presence of antidiuretic hormone (ADH), which makes the collecting ducts more permeable to water, allowing water to move out of the ducts and into the hyperosmolar medulla.
options: (2) Maintaining hyperosmolarity towards inner medullary interstitium in the kidneys.
(3) Secretion of erythropoietin by juxtaglomerular complex.

blocks.question:
Arrange the events of Renin - Angiotensin mechanism in correct sequence.

(A) Activation of JG cells and release of renin.

(B) Angiotensin II activates release of aldosterone.

(C) Fall in glomerular blood pressure.

(D) Reabsorption of Na+ and water from distal convoluted tubule.

(E) Angiotensinogen is converted to Angiotensin I and then to Angiotensin II.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

(1) (C), (A), (E), (B), (D)

(2) (A), (D), (E), (C), (B)

(3) (A), (D), (C), (B), (E)

(4) (B), (A), (E), (D), ( C)
options: (A) Activation of JG cells and release of renin.
(B) Angiotensin II activates release of aldosterone.
(D) Reabsorption of Na+ and water from distal convoluted tubule.

blocks.title: Question.2
blocks.question:
Erythropoietin hormone which stimulates R.B.C. formation is produced by :-

(1) Alpha cells of pancreas

(2) The cells of rostral adenohypophysis

(3) The cells of bone marrow

(4) Juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney         (NEET (UG) 2021)
blocks.answer:
Answer = 4

Explanation:

The Renin-Angiotensin mechanism is a series of events triggered by a fall in blood pressure or low sodium levels, which helps to regulate blood pressure and fluid balance. The correct sequence of events is as follows:

  • (C) Fall in glomerular blood pressure:
This initiates the process. A drop in blood pressure is detected by specialized cells in the kidney.
  • (A) Activation of JG cells and release of renin:
The juxtaglomerular (JG) cells in the kidneys release renin in response to the low blood pressure.
  • (E) Angiotensinogen is converted to Angiotensin I and then to Angiotensin II:
Renin converts angiotensinogen (produced by the liver) into angiotensin I, which is then converted into angiotensin II by the enzyme ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) found mainly in the lungs.
  • (B) Angiotensin II activates release of aldosterone:
Angiotensin II stimulates the adrenal glands to release aldosterone, a hormone that helps increase sodium and water reabsorption.
  • (D) Reabsorption of Na+ and water from distal convoluted tubule:
Aldosterone acts on the distal convoluted tubule and collecting ducts of the kidneys, promoting the reabsorption of sodium (Na+) and water, which increases blood volume and raises blood pressure.

blocks.title: Question.1
blocks.question:
What will happen if the stretch receptors of the urinary bladder wall are  totally removed?

(1) There will be no micturition

(2) Urine will not collect in the bladder

(3) Micturition will continue

(4) Urine will continue to collect normally in the bladder
blocks.answer:
Answer = 4

Explanation:

The stretch receptors in the wall of the urinary bladder are responsible for detecting the volume of urine as it accumulates. They send signals to the brain to initiate the micturition reflex when the bladder reaches a certain level of fullness.
options: (2) Urine will not collect in the bladder
(4) Urine will continue to collect normally in the bladder

blocks.title: Question.2
blocks.question:
Haemodialysis helps in the patient having :-

(1) Uremia

(2) Anaemia

(3) Diabetes

(4) Goitre
blocks.answer:
The correct answer is:
(1) Uremia

Explanation:

Haemodialysis is a medical procedure used to treat uremia, which occurs when the kidneys are no longer able to filter waste products, such as urea, from the blood. This can happen due to kidney failure. During haemodialysis, a machine filters the blood to remove these waste products and excess fluid, which helps to maintain the balance of chemicals in the body and prevent the buildup of toxins.

blocks.title: Question.3
blocks.question:
Blood dialysis is called :-

(1) Artificial lung

(2) Artificial kidney

(3) Artificial heart

(4) Artificial brain
blocks.answer:
Ans= 2

Explanation:

Blood dialysis is commonly referred to as the process of using an artificial kidney. During this process, a machine performs the function of the kidneys by filtering waste products, excess fluids, and toxins from the blood in cases of kidney failure. The machine, known as a dialysis machine, mimics the natural filtration process of the kidneys, helping patients with kidney dysfunction maintain the proper balance of fluids and electrolytes.

blocks.title: Disorders of Excretory System
blocks.text:
(i) Uremia : Presence of excess urea in blood. Malfunctioning of kidneys can

lead to accumulation of urea in blood, a condition called uremia, which is

highly harmful and may lead to kidney failure.

(ii) Renal failure : It is a syndrome characterised by renal dysfunction,

oliguria, anuria, sudden rise in metabolic waste products like urea &

creatinine in blood (Uremia). It is either of acute (sudden onset) or chronic

(slow onset) nature.

Kidney transplantation is the ultimate method in the correction of renal

failures (kidney failure).

(iii) Renal calculi (Urolithiasis) : Formation of stone within kidney. These

calculi are made of calcium phosphate, uric acid., cystine or calcium Oxalate.

(iv) Glomerulonephritis : It is a disease where due to infection or injury in

the basement membrane, the inflammation of glomerulu  progressively lead

to renal failure and death.

(v) Glycosuria :- Excretion of Glucose through Urine. This sign is present in Diabetes-mellitus. This disease is caused mainly due to less secretion of Insulin.
